review: 1:1 בַּעֲדִי אָנִי? כֵּן, בַּעֲדִי — the Arabic عَنِّي أَنَا؟! نَعَمْ عَنِّي is a question and its answer inside one line; Hebrew keeps both halves and the exclamation, because the whole hymn rests on that turn from doubt to assurance.
3:1 הֲבַעֲדִי הִרְכִּין רֹאשׁוֹ — John 19:30 (וַיֵּט רֹאשׁוֹ); the Arabic هَلْ عَنِّي رَأْسَهُ حَنَى is that bowing of the head, and Hebrew keeps the question form of the stanza.

3:3–3:4 בַּעֲדִי הַפְּדוּת הִשְׁלִים / וְנָתַן שָׁלוֹם בְּחֵן — John 19:30 (נִשְׁלַם) with the peace-gift of John 14:27; the Arabic عَنِّي الْفِدَاءَ تَمَّمَ / أَعْطَى السَّلَامَ مُنْعِمًا joins the finished redemption to the free peace, and Hebrew keeps the pair.
1:2 אַהֲבָתוֹ לִי נִשְׂגָּבָה — 'His love for me is exalted', for حُبُّهُ لِي سَامٍ عَجِيب; the Arabic has two adjectives and the line holds one, so נִשְׂגָּב carries both the height and the wonder.
